_comment: Note 655's shape with synthetic names: two children in one exchange, a different observation about each. The transcript joins the two children in ONE clause, which note 655's own wording does not — its comma is removed on purpose, so the fixture tests the shared clause rather than a boundary the model can simply find. Green since #120: the prompt's span arithmetic carries an exception for this shape, the model returns a span per child at the same start, and AssembleNotes derives each span's end from the next greater start, so two spans hold the one clause with a summary each. Measured 25 runs of 25 on mistral-medium-2508 and 21 of 25 on gpt-5.4-mini; without the exception gpt-5.4-mini scored 0 of 25. This fixture is the guard on that sentence: it goes red if a model merges the clause into one span with both labels, which gives each child the other's observation (the #99 bleed), and red again if Go goes back to rejecting a repeated start, which fails the whole job. Nadia and Bruno are far apart phonetically on purpose: the only thing this fixture can fail on is the merge, never name resolution. The 'colours' sentence belongs to the two children named, not the class (#151): 'they both' points back to Nadia and Bruno. Théa is on the roster and never named, so she gets no note; she is left out of expected_students on purpose, because listing her would fail recall on a correct run. Precision is the guard instead: if the model reads the sentence as 'group', the fan-out gives Théa a note and precision drops to 2/3, under the 0.7 pass mark. That margin holds only with exactly two expected students: a third would let a phantom pass at 3/4.
